name: example-parallel-implement-review-quickstart-salary-range
goal: Demonstrate a real parallel implementer run plus reviewed promotion for a new salary-range quickstart endpoint.

sharedContext.summary: Add a new quickstart endpoint `GET /api/employees/by-salary-range?minSalary=100000&maxSalary=140000&limit=2` that returns `EmployeeView` rows within the inclusive salary range, ordered by salary descending. Keep `limit` defaulting to 10 and capped at 25. Clamp `minSalary` to zero and ensure `maxSalary` is at least `minSalary` before executing the query.
constraints: Keep work bounded to the Spring Boot starter quickstart example.
Do not edit TODO.md, ai/state files, ai/log files, or ai/indexes.
Task write scopes must stay disjoint so the two implementers can run in parallel.

tasks.title: Implement the quickstart salary-range endpoint
tasks.prompt: Implement `GET /api/employees/by-salary-range`. Reuse the existing in-memory employee dataset and return `EmployeeView` rows with salary between `minSalary` and `maxSalary` inclusive, sorted by salary descending, with `limit` defaulting to 10 and capped at 25. Clamp `minSalary` to zero and ensure `maxSalary` is at least `minSalary` before executing the query.

tasks.title: Document and test the quickstart salary-range endpoint
tasks.prompt: Using the shared endpoint contract, update the quickstart README curl examples and add focused default plus virtual-thread integration coverage for `GET /api/employees/by-salary-range?minSalary=100000&maxSalary=140000&limit=2`. Cover inclusive range filtering, salary-desc ordering, default limit behavior, and maxSalary normalization when it is below minSalary.

tasks.title: Review the combined quickstart salary-range change
tasks.prompt: Review the combined quickstart salary-range endpoint change for correctness, test sufficiency, and whether the README contract matches the implementation. Focus on regressions, missing validation, and promotion risks.
